study.question: Do same-field target/history products help beyond term count and per-event product magnitude, and can a fixed parameter-free product normalization improve the current validation reference? Observed raw D AUC=0.6144940344272417, Logloss=0.19669042580912716 versus ordinary adapter 0.6133310797329501/0.19686922674369595. Cross-removal alone gives 0.614296838626921/0.19667252436933869, so the joint restriction has an AUC/Logloss tradeoff. At the joint checkpoint the ordered first-512 diagnostic gives D norm 5.60816 versus ordinary-product norm 10.98643; this is a candidate-authored activity observation, not population or causal evidence. Current train_seed=42 has no exposed override: this bounded replacement pilot is exploratory and does not fulfill the prior conditional paired-seed recommendation.
study.hypothesis: H1 (performance, provisional): suppressing event-dependent magnitude of the explicit product block may regularize noisy target/history scale and improve AUC at unchanged trainable capacity; this is unproven, and useful intensity may instead be lost. H2 (attribution, provisional): if explicit same-field direction matters beyond raw product norm and term count, N(D) should outperform N(X) under identical normalization. These hypotheses are separate: a normalization gain does not establish semantic alignment. No saturation, event-relevance or novelty claim is made.

nearest_work.difference: Local raw-D restriction is inherited, not invented here. Constructor, encoding, mask/normalization and classifier helpers are reused exactly by AST. Source/aggregate replay identity does not certify common-state tensors or robustness across seeds.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/2210.15154v1; AutoAttention v1, 2022-10-27, sections III-A/III-B, equations 5-6 and Algorithm 1
nearest_work.difference: Primary method learns field-pair scalar strengths in target-behavior dot-product attention and iteratively prunes them. Field-pair selection/noisy interactions are established prior work. Here a fixed two-term vector product occupies one input block of an existing MLP scorer; there is no learned pair weighting/pruning, additional query field or pruning schedule. The local normalization/replacement test is not an AutoAttention reproduction or a priority claim.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/1706.06978v4; DIN v4, 2018-09-13, section 4.3, equation 3 and following text
nearest_work.difference: Candidate-conditioned history aggregation is inherited background. The primary DIN text relaxes unit-sum activation weights; the frozen local adaptation uses masked softmax. This study keeps that local softmax and changes only its explicit product input; no exact DIN reproduction is claimed.

DIF-SR generates separate attribute attention matrices and fuses them for sequential recommendation, with item-value representation and auxiliary predictors. Here query/history/value sums and the original MLP scorer remain fused; only a vector product input is normalized or re-paired. No transferred rank, gradient-flexibility or performance theorem is asserted.

FiBiNET uses learned bilinear field interactions and feature reweighting. This candidate adds neither learned matrices nor SENET; it normalizes an inherited fixed Hadamard-product sum. Field interaction modeling is established background.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/2010.04245v1; Query-Key Normalization v1, 2020-10-08, section 2 equation 2 and section 3
nearest_work.difference: QKNorm normalizes query/key vectors before dot-product attention and uses a learned scale. Here the sum of two Hadamard products is normalized after multiplication, with no learned scale, while other MLP input blocks retain their norms. Normalization in attention is established; this local intervention is not QKNorm or a novelty claim.

study.proposed_difference: Three standalone modules complete the 2x2 without an unchanged seed-42 replay: normalized_aligned is N(D); crossed_raw is X; crossed_unit is N(X). D=qc*hc+qb*hb and X=qc*hb+qb*hc, using only existing category/brand embeddings and both with target-action/recency products omitted. N normalizes each event along its 16-dimensional product axis to L2 norm 1 above a fixed 1e-3 denominator floor. Clamp squared norm before sqrt, propagate gradients through the denominator, leave zero input at zero. No input, parameter, optimizer/loss, schedule, data, seed, mask, history value or scorer change. New configuration keys select only these two factors; no alpha/floor/temperature sweep. Train from scratch only through the automatic host interface after this proposal; no local training.
predictions: H1 predicts normalized_aligned minus raw-D full-validation AUC > 0. Logloss is reported separately; worsened Logloss makes this a ranking/probability-loss tradeoff. This is a predeclared directional prediction, not a significance threshold.

H2 predicts aligned minus crossed AUC > 0 at unit normalization, with the raw pairing contrast as context. Crossed products can still capture semantic correlations; this tests explicit field pairing, not removal of all semantic information.

By construction each nonfloored unit product has norm 1, padded events have zero attention, all-masked rows have zero summaries, and helper/forward logits should agree at the same checkpoint. Diagnostics report support/floor counts and centered score deltas; these invariants must pass before attribution.

Report all four cells, AUC and Logloss simple effects, factorial interaction and measured host costs, including negative/failed outcomes. Any slices are exploratory with supplied sample/positive/negative counts and training-defined bins; no new subgroup-driven gate or selection rule.

If raw pairing preference disappears under common norms while the implementation is valid, scale/geometry dependence becomes more plausible. This pattern cannot by itself establish mediation or identify a unique mechanism.
falsifiers: H1 is not supported at this recipe if N(D) AUC is <= raw D; preserve null/worse results and do not automatically tune a scale or floor to rescue it.
H2 is weakened if N(X) matches or beats N(D), or any raw-D advantage vanishes at matched nonfloored norms. Equal term count/norm does not remove all possible geometric or optimization explanations.

Nonfinite logits/diagnostics/gradients, padding mass, nonzero empty summaries, helper/forward disagreement, material norm mismatch above floor or unintended parameter/initialization differences invalidate the corresponding attribution. Treat execution failures separately from scientific negatives.

AUC gains confined to tiny exploratory slices, signs that reverse under later authorized paired seeds, or improved diagnostics with no primary metric benefit do not justify mechanism or robust-performance claims.
No independent-seed or closed-assessment result exists for these modules. Single-seed improvements cannot establish significance, novelty, production generalization or equal-compute superiority.
